sections.heading: Quick Answer
sections.html: Dental implants can last many years with the right planning and maintenance, but no dentist can promise a lifetime result. Long-term success depends on bone support, gum health, bite forces, medical history, home care, and regular dental visits.

sections.heading: What Affects Implant Longevity?
sections.html:
The implant, abutment, and final crown or bridge all have different maintenance needs. A healthy foundation, a well-designed bite, and good cleaning habits help protect the result over time.

  • Gum and bone health
  • Smoking or medical conditions that affect healing
  • Grinding or heavy bite forces
  • Quality of the final crown, bridge, or denture
  • Regular professional maintenance

sections.heading: When to Schedule an Implant Consultation
sections.html: If you are missing a tooth, have a failing tooth, or are frustrated with a loose denture, an exam and imaging can help clarify your options. Elm Ridge Implant and Family Dentistry can review whether a single implant, implant bridge, snap-on denture, or full-arch plan makes sense.

faq.question: Can dental implants last a lifetime?
faq.answer: Some implants last for decades, but lifetime results cannot be guaranteed. Health, hygiene, bite forces, and maintenance all matter.

faq.question: Do implant crowns ever need to be replaced?
faq.answer: Yes, the crown or prosthetic tooth may wear, chip, loosen, or need replacement even when the implant itself remains healthy.
